title: The configuration-rollback writes, the four target kinds, the version-before rule, the act date, the right that opens it and the two record codes are not in the sources, and the feature is already carried by another P4 story
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3.md (RWB-E8-011); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6/Recovery Workbench FSD P4 Access and administration v3.md (A2.3, A2.22); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v5/Recovery Workbench TSD P4 Access and administration v3.md (T3.0, T3.1, T3.2, T4, T6.1, T6.3, T-A); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Business Requirements Program v4.md (5.3, 5.4, 5.7); _work/msr/extract/B-REQ-PRD-S9/Recovery Workbench Business Requirements Epics 3 to 8 v1.md (8.6, BR-073, RULE-001); 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Business Rules and Routing Logic v4.md (R-UNI-38, R-UNI-39); _work/msr/context/P4.md (ownership rows of P4)
description: Six values of this key are absent from the sources and one is a scope conflict. (1) The writes: neither the FSD nor the TSD names an operation that rolls back a version of a table of rwb-access; the legacy endpoints are the rule-version paths of rwb-decision and the reference-load rollback of rwb-case, and this story fixes POST /api/recovery/access/v1/admin/config-rollbacks and its read GET .../{rollbackId}. (2) The target set: the legacy story says any versioned table, and TSD P4 v3 T3.1 gives a version column to permission (matrix_version), masking_rule (masking_version), role_conflict (conflict_version) and delegation_limit (limit_version) only; role carries none, so the story fixes four target kinds and leaves role rows alone. (3) The version-before rule: no source says how the earlier version of a table is found, and permission has no date column at all. (4) The act date: no source says whether a rollback is dated now or submitted, and the request field set carrying a date is not defined. (5) The right: the legacy permission table gives Rules and parameters C to RW-COE and A to RW-RISK, TSD P4 v3 T6.1 gives RW-COE CRUD in Rules and parameters and CRUD in Platform administration to RW-PLATADM with R in Rules and parameters, and the FSD makes the Platform administrator the primary actor, so three sources disagree on what letter opens the rollback in which area. (6) The record: the two decision-record codes of the withdrawal and the restoration, the record codes' field placement and the text of MSG-P3-015 are not stated. (7) Scope: FEAT-ADM-06 Roll back a configuration version is claimed by RWB-P4-AD013-APP, which gates the rollback of rule package versions (P7) and reference-data versions (P3); this story carries the same feature for the tables rwb-access owns, and the split between the two is a decision of this Work Package and not of a source.
evidence: RWB-E8-011 gives one story sentence, two acceptance criteria (AC1 returns any versioned table to its previous version and records the rollback with the rule version; AC2 nothing changes with MSG-P7-003 when the decision log cannot be written) and two rule-version endpoints, both of which are rwb-decision's now. FSD P4 v3 A2.22 repeats the intent, the metric and BR-P4-022 with no operation, no field and no state; A2.3 AC-ALT-P4-003-01 gives the only worked rollback and its record-ID rule for the queue table, and AC-EXC-P4-003-02 gives MSG-P3-015 for a table with no earlier version, without a text. TSD P4 v3 T3.1 lists the columns of the four tables and T3.2 the seven values of LOV-VERSION-STATUS, T4 gives a lifecycle for a rule package version only, T6.1 gives the letter matrix, T6.3 says a load, an approval and a rollback each write one append-only change-log entry, and appendix T-A lists no rollback of a table of this service. The Temporal and Drools design and Architecture v5 slides 14 and 41 name no rollback of an access table. RWB-P4-AD013-APP and RWB-P4-AD013-CON already carry FEAT-ADM-06 for the two owner tables.
proposed: Keep the two paths, the four target kinds and the two operations proposed by RWB-P4-E8011-CON, freeze them at the contract review with the security administrator, the CoE analyst and the P7 and P3 tech leads, and record in the Service Contract Catalog that FEAT-ADM-06 is carried twice: by RWB-P4-E8011 for the tables rwb-access owns and by RWB-P4-AD013 for the rule and reference versions of the two other owners.
